lead.headline: A Radar Plane Takes Up Watch Over Poland
lead.deck: NATO has sent a plane with a giant spinning radar to Poland, after three Russian missiles crashed on Polish ground.
body: Poland is in central Europe, next to Ukraine. On 20 November, Poland's prosecutors say, three Russian cruise missiles crashed on Polish land. Poland belongs to NATO, a group of countries that protect one another.

Three days later, NATO answered. NATO's European commander, General Alexus Grynkewich, approved sending a special plane. It is called an AWACS, short for airborne early warning and control system, and it carries a spinning radar dome about 9 metres across.
Why put a radar on a plane? Radar on the ground can be blocked by the curve of the Earth and by hills. A radar flying high can see much farther.
NATO's fleet of these planes is based in Gelsenkirchen, a city in Germany.

world.headline: India's Farms Grow a Record Pile of Grain
world.deck: New government figures say India grew more grain in the year 2025-26 than ever before.
body: India's farmers grew 378.538 million tonnes of foodgrain in the year 2025-26. Foodgrain means crops like rice, wheat and maize that people and animals eat. The year before, it was 357.732 million tonnes.
Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan shared the figures in New Delhi on Thursday.
Rice led the way with 155.154 million tonnes, up from 150.184 million. Wheat came to 122.064 million tonnes. Maize jumped from 43.409 million tonnes to 55.025 million tonnes.
Rice sales abroad also grew by five per cent.

quiz.why: The paper says AWACS is short for airborne early warning and control system.

quiz.q: Where is NATO's AWACS fleet based?
quiz.why: The fleet is based in Gelsenkirchen, Germany.

quiz.q: How much foodgrain did India grow in 2025-26?
quiz.why: The figure for 2025-26 was 378.538 million tonnes.

quiz.q: Which crop was the biggest of rice, wheat and maize?
quiz.why: Rice made 155.154 million tonnes, the most of the three.

fact_or_fiction.claim: Three Russian cruise missiles crashed in Poland on 20 November, say Polish prosecutors.
fact_or_fiction.why: The Polish prosecutor's office said this.

fact_or_fiction.claim: A radar flying high can see less far than a radar on the ground.
fact_or_fiction.why: Flying high lets the radar see farther, because the Earth's curve and hills can block ground radar.

fact_or_fiction.claim: India's rice sales abroad grew by five per cent.
fact_or_fiction.why: Rice exports rose five per cent, says the report.

numbers.q: About how wide is the spinning radar dome on NATO's AWACS planes?
numbers.why: The dome is about 9 metres across.

numbers.q: How many million tonnes of rice did India grow in 2025-26 (to the nearest whole number)?
numbers.why: The report gives 155.154 million tonnes of rice.
